WY_Basin_Use = (await FileAttachment("Data/WaterYear_Basin_Sum.csv").csv()).map(d =>({

Supply = (await FileAttachment("Data/Supply.csv").csv()).map(d =>({
  ...d,
  Water_Year: String(d.Water_Year),
  Date: new Date(d.Date),
  Supply_Acre_Feet: +d.Acre_Feet,
  Supply_MAF: parseFloat((+d.Million_Acre_Feet).toFixed(2)),
  Upper_Basin_Supply: +d.Upper_Basin_Supply, // Made by subtracting 8.25 maf (7.5 to LB and half of 1.5 to Mexico) to reflect legal supply available to Upper Basin

  LB_10yr_Avg: parseFloat((+d.LB_10yr_Avg).toFixed(2))
})).sort((a, b) => a.Date - b.Date)

SNOTEL = (await FileAttachment("Data/Snow Water Equivalent.csv").csv()).map(d => {
    const date  = new Date(d.Snow_Date + "T00:00:00")
    const month = date.getUTCMonth()

    return {
        ...d,
        Date: date, 
        Normalized_Date: new Date(Date.UTC(
            month >= 9 ? 2000 : 2001,
            month,
            date.getUTCDate()
        )),
        Calendar_Year: d.Calendar_Year,
        Snow_Year: d.Snow_Year,
        HUC6: d.HUC6,
        Minimum: +d.Min,
        Maximum: +d.Max,
        Median_91_20: +d.Median_91_20,
        Average_SWE: +d.Average_SWE
        }
}).sort((a, b) => a.Normalized_Date - b.Normalized_Date)







SNOTEL_Filtered = SNOTEL.filter(d => d.HUC6 === Basin_Select)

d3

{

    reverse: false,
    fillOpacity: 0.9,
    strokeWidth: 0.3,
    leg_title: "SWE inches",
    tip: true
  });

}

About
text:
The Colorado River Atlas is an effort to make information about the history and status of the Colorado River Basin available to the public.
Existing data resources can often be difficult to access and analyze for the general public, making critical information about the history and future of the United State’s most over stressed river out of reach for many. As reservoir levels continue to fall and long-term management of the river remains tenuous, public accessibility to this information becomes increasingly important.
This project seeks to make this information easier to access and interact with, giving people an important resource to inform themselves and others about the challenges facing the Colorado. It began as a personal project, filling in gaps in data presentation and consolidating different resources into one place, and is aiming to grow to include more resources on water usage, land use patterns, water conservation efforts, legal and political issues, science, history and more.
The CRA is built using Quarto, an open-source scientific and technical publishing system, and published through GitHub Pages. Click on the GitHub icon in the top-right to visit the GitHub repository and explore the scripts used to process data and build the site.


Want to contribute to this project? Visit the GitHub repo and make a pull request or use the email below to get in contact with your ideas.



Send an email to coloradoriveratlas@gmail.com to get in contact with questions, comments and submissions.

Surface water extent data is from the JRC Global Surface Water Dataset, using satellite data to map surface water from 1984 to 2020. Years after 2020 are created using data from the Sentinel-2 satellite through the OpenEO API. Normalized Difference Water Index was calculated and vectorized to create polygons of surface water extent for included reservoirs, using the median value for each pixel across the entire year. The current year is the median of the past two months to approximate current levels and account for discrepencies and cloud cover in individual collections.
